correctness.rationale: For P(t)=t(t+1)(2t+1)/6, the definition is equivalent for all positive n,r,a,b to (a+b)P(n)=bP(n+r). With (a,b)=(563,11), gcd(563,11)=1, P(5)=55, P(20)=2870, P(142)=964535, P(532)=50331190; the two equalities 574*55=11*2870=31570 and 574*964535=11*50331190=553643090 prove both n=5,r=15 and n=142,r=390. The exact arbitrary-precision checker uses independent direct sums and closed-form calculations. For the associated projective cubic, the displayed partial derivatives have no common projective zero, showing smoothness, and (11:41:1) is a rational point. No infinite enumeration or completeness claim is made.

originality.rationale: The claim is deliberately narrower than mere existence of two square-cobalancing indices. An explicitly published 2024 OEIS square-pyramidal product identity already yields examples with right coefficient b=1 and an index n=1; those are recognized as covered and not promoted. The new exact certificate has coprime coefficients (563,11), b>1, and both distinct indices n>1, with a repeated 574:11 square-pyramidal ratio not given or implied by the inspected product-of-pyramidal identities. The initiating paper (2022) asks about multiplicity but does not prove this example; its plotted coefficient range stops at 120. Direct searches of mathematical-records and accessible prior claims did not find the same primitive nondegenerate pair. Novelty remains contingent on unindexed literature.

value.rationale: The motivating 2022 paper explicitly asks whether any fixed coprime square-cobalancing weights admit more than one index. Known product-based witnesses with b=1 and n=1 leave the natural nondegenerate case open; the explicit primitive (563,11) certificate proves multiplicity survives even when b>1 and both n>1. That exact boundary matters because it excludes trivial constructions and reveals two positive integral points on an associated smooth genus-one cubic. It is a mathematically motivated counterexample, not an arbitrary numerical slice; no general downstream classification is claimed.
